source_video: out/log_full_nocaptions.mp4 (preferred). Fallback: the captioned upload, cropped (see shorts_brief.md section 1).

cut_rule.end: last_take.speech_end_s + 0.12 (never include the pause after the last take)

clips.headline: Can paper reach the Moon?
clips.why: Best hook. Question first, then jump straight to the mental-math answer (42). Ends on the big 42.
clips.yt_title: How Many Folds Reach the Moon? (Do It in Your Head)
clips.risk: t36 and t38 had text cut off at the frame edges in the full video. Check frames; if still cut off, do NOT publish this clip until S6 is fixed.

clips.headline: What does a log actually mean?
clips.why: The definition plus the 'pause and try one' challenge (log base 2 of 32 = 5). Good for comments.
clips.yt_title: What Is a Log? Try This One Without a Calculator
clips.risk: Starts mid-explanation (t09 begins 'That's a log'), so the headline must carry the context.

clips.headline: Why do so many numbers start with 1?
clips.why: Strong curiosity story: Benford bars, Newcomb's worn pages, then the log ruler answer.
clips.yt_title: Why Do So Many Numbers Start With 1?
clips.risk: None known. Ends on 'under five percent' (the ruler payoff).

clips.headline: The same math hides in earthquakes, acid and sound
clips.why: Three real-world examples, very visual (seismograph, pH tiles, dB).
clips.yt_title: Earthquakes, pH and Sound Use the Same Trick
clips.risk: Starts at 'Earthquakes.' (t31); t30 is skipped on purpose because it refers to the log ruler.

clips.headline: The graph that never stops climbing
clips.why: Mirror-image curves. Abstract, so lowest priority. Make it last or skip.
clips.yt_title: The Log Graph Explained in 45 Seconds
clips.risk: Visuals are thin lines; small on a letterboxed phone screen.

do_not_make: Do not make horizontal (16:9) clips: YouTube never counts them as Shorts and Instagram shrinks them.
No subscribe or call-to-action text in any clip.
Do not mention binary search, merge sort or sorting anywhere.
